questions.prompt: Which change is binary-compatible for callers of a pimpl class?
options: Changing a public method's parameter type
Adding a public data member
Adding a data member to the hidden Impl struct
Adding a virtual function to the public class
questions.explanation: The public class is only a pointer; its size and layout do not change.

questions.prompt: Why can a std::string in the signature of a prebuilt .so cause a link error with a different compiler setting?
options: The linker forbids templates such as std::string in the signature of a .so
Strings cannot be exported from a shared library, only char pointers can
The mangled type name and layout differ between library ABIs (libstdc++ dual ABI)
std::string is not copyable, so it cannot cross a shared library boundary
questions.explanation: GCC's _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI switches std::string between two incompatible types with different mangled names.

questions.prompt: Which return type states exclusive ownership transfer most clearly in C++?
options: Map& (a mutable reference)
const Map& (a const reference)
Map* (a raw pointer)
std::unique_ptr<Map>
questions.explanation: unique_ptr documents and enforces that the caller becomes the sole owner.

questions.prompt: A function returns std::string::c_str() of a local string through an extern "C" interface. What is wrong?
options: c_str() allocates memory that is never freed
extern "C" forbids strings
The pointer dangles after the function returns
It is fine: strings live forever
questions.explanation: The local string is destroyed at return; return static storage or write into a caller buffer.

questions.prompt: struct Pose { double x; double y; } is 16 bytes. Version 2 adds a double z and an int flag at the end. With natural alignment on x86-64, what is the new sizeof? Give an integer.
questions.explanation: 3 doubles = 24 bytes, int at offset 24, padded to 32.

questions.prompt: A library has 9 exported symbols; 6 are extern "C". How many are mangled? Integer.

An application compiled against a struct with fields (int size; double x; double y) = 24 bytes receives a v2 struct (int size; double x; double y; double z) = 32 bytes. If the library honours the caller's size field and fills only the fields that fit, how many bytes of the caller's struct are written at most? Integer.
questions.explanation: The library limits itself to the caller-declared 24 bytes, so no overflow occurs.

questions.prompt: A test hook rc_live_arms() returns 0 initially. A test creates 3 Arm objects, moves one into another, and destroys one by scope exit. How many arms remain alive if the moved-to object previously owned an arm that should be released? Start: a, b, c created; c = std::move(a); then b goes out of scope. Integer.
questions.explanation: Three created; move assignment c = std::move(a) destroys c's old arm (2 alive: a's arm now in c, b's); b leaves scope: 1 alive.

questions.prompt: Declare a pimpl class Planner so that a user translation unit including only the header compiles. Which special members must be declared in the header and defined in the .cpp?
rubric: class Planner { public: Planner(); ~Planner(); Planner(Planner&&) noexcept; Planner& operator=(Planner&&) noexcept; private: struct Impl; std::unique_ptr<Impl> impl_; };
Destructor and moves are defined in the .cpp (= default) where Impl is complete.
Reason: unique_ptr's deleter needs the complete type, otherwise 'invalid application of sizeof to incomplete type'.

questions.prompt: On x86-64 Linux (Itanium ABI) let struct A { double d; char b; ~A(); }; struct B : A { char c; char e; };. What is the byte offset of B::c? Give an integer.
questions.explanation: A has a user-provided destructor, so it is not a POD for layout: d at 0..7, b at 8, dsize(A)=9, sizeof(A)=16. The next subobject of B starts at dsize(A)=9, reusing the tail padding, so c is at offset 9 and e at 10; sizeof(B)=16 (measured with g++: 16 16 9). Had A been a POD, c would sit at offset 16.

questions.prompt: A library built with -D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=0 exports int get_id(const Config&), where struct Config { std::string name; int id; };. An application built with the default (new) ABI calls it. What happens?
options: The linker reports an undefined reference because std::string differs between the two ABIs
The program links, but get_id reads id at the wrong offset because sizeof(std::string) is 8 in one ABI and 32 in the other
The program links and runs correctly because the symbol get_id and the name Config are identical
The compiler rejects the call because the old and new std::string are not convertible
questions.explanation: Config is a user type, so the mangled name _Z6get_idRK6Config is the same in both builds and the linker is satisfied (the std::string appears in the signature only when it is a parameter or return type). The layouts differ: the old COW std::string is one 8-byte pointer, the new one is 32 bytes, so id is at offset 8 in the library but 32 in the application. In the experiment the application stored 42 at offset 32 and get_id returned 3, the string length that sits at offset 8 of the new layout.

questions.prompt: Your exported polymorphic class Sensor (virtual read(), virtual reset()) is derived from by client plugins that you do not recompile. Propose how to add a new capability calibrate() in version 2 without breaking old plugins, and justify it from the vtable layout.
rubric: Do not insert or append a virtual function to Sensor: the vtable slots are fixed at compile time from the header, and client vtables built against version 1 would not contain the new slot (or would shift the slots of virtuals declared in derived classes), so a call lands in the wrong function.

Add the capability outside the existing vtable: a new interface class (for example Calibratable) that plugins opt into, discovered with dynamic_cast or a query function, or a non-virtual Sensor::calibrate() forwarding to a hidden implementation, or a new C function.

Mention that adding a virtual function is only safe for a class with no derived classes outside the library, otherwise the SONAME must change; an opaque handle plus a function table with a size field avoids the issue.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
